summary.title: 21 Lessons from 14 Years at Google
summary.one_liner: Twenty-one non-technical lessons on career growth, collaboration, and engineering judgment drawn from 14 years at Google.
takeaways: Engineers who thrive focus on user problems, alignment, and people as much as on writing code.
Clarity, deletion of unneeded work, and boring technology choices reduce operational risk and cost.
Visibility of impact and a strong professional network matter as much as the work itself.
Metrics get gamed and glue work can stall careers unless it is timeboxed and made visible.
Slow projects are usually misalignment problems; admitting uncertainty and seeking real agreement helps teams learn.
summary.summary: A personal essay by an engineer who spent about 14 years at Google, presented as 21 numbered lessons. The lessons cover topics such as user obsession, alignment over being right, shipping early, clarity in code, managing technology novelty, self-advocacy, glue work, metrics, networking, and time management. It is written as opinion and reflection rather than a tutorial, with no specific technologies or step-by-step methods, and it ends with a short closing thought on curiosity and humility.
